rows.title: Policy
rows.read: Britain's hotter inflation figure makes a Bank of England hike in November close to certain, and an Australian central banker pushed hike bets higher there too. Canada and New Zealand are also expected to raise rates this month, while the Fed holds until December. Currencies whose central banks are about to act keep the rate edge.
rows.figure: BoE Nov 5 hike ~95%; RBA Nov 3 ~40% (Reuters); BoC Oct 28 ~85–89%; RBNZ Oct 28 ~80%; Fed Oct hold ~84%, Dec hike ~90%; ECB Dec ~84%; BoJ Dec ~73%

rows.title: Growth
rows.read: Japan's exports grew more slowly than expected, a sign that strong chip demand is not fully offsetting other weakness. US housing remains under pressure from high mortgage rates. Neither changed the rate outlook overnight.
rows.figure: Japan Sep exports +16.7% y/y (~+20% fc), deficit ¥537B (¥181B fc); US housing starts 1.22M (1.30M fc); pending home sales -7.3%

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: UK inflation rose more than expected as energy costs fed through, showing the oil shock is still lifting prices. That keeps pressure on central banks to hike rather than wait. Coming up: New Zealand's inflation report at 4:45 PM CT today.
rows.figure: UK CPI Sep 3.5% y/y (3.4% fc; Aug 3.1%; BoE July forecast 3.0%); NZ Q3 CPI fc 3.8% y/y (prior 4.1%), 4:45 PM CT

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: Markets were calm overnight even as tanker attacks reportedly spread into the Gulf of Oman. Hopes for US–Iran diplomacy are holding up without any confirmation, so safe-haven currencies got no fresh lift.
rows.figure: Dollar index ~101.8, near a three-week low; US–Iran framework still unconfirmed; ≥18 vessels attacked in two weeks (Kpler)

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.read: Oil climbed back toward $110 as Gulf shipping risks widened. That helps exporters like Canada and costs importers like Japan, the euro area and Britain, where higher energy bills are already showing up in inflation.
rows.figure: Brent ~$110 (Reuters $109.64, +0.8%); WTI ~$98.7; gold ~$4,115 (-0.3%); Japan mineral-fuel import bill still heavy

rows.title: Positioning
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, even as a Bank of Canada hike looks likely, which leaves those bets exposed if the loonie keeps rising. They also bet against the kiwi and the euro. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against EUR and NZD (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), strongly for gold (trimmed); oil bets near weakest since 2015

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.read: France's budget fight is on hold until a revenue vote on October 27, with a Moody's review of France on Friday, so the risk to the euro lingers. In Britain, hotter inflation raises the cost of help with energy bills in next week's budget.
rows.figure: France revenue vote Oct 27 (formal vote Nov 3); Moody's on France Fri Oct 23; UK budget Oct 28
